lines.latin: al-Mamlaka al-'Arabiya as-Sa'udiya (Kingdom of Saudi Arabia)

notes: 1959 colour slide of a painted wooden board on the Dhahran air terminal (now King Abdulaziz Air Base), photographed from below at an angle; the left edge crops the first D of the first two English lines. The Arabic is in Naskh with shadda and other vowel marks, omitted here. Two palm-and-swords emblems flank the text.

author: عمرو
attribution: Photo: عمرو, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Makkah_highway_sign.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Overhead gantry on the Jeddah-Makkah highway, shot through a windscreen (scratches, rear-view mirror at top right). Left panel: green 'Muslims only' box, Makkah with Kaaba pictogram; right panel: red 'For Non Muslims' box. Small route shields under the arrows (Arabic-Indic numbers, one possibly ٢٨٨) are too small to read reliably and are not transcribed. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.

lines.text: شارع الأمير حمود بن عبد العزيز
lines.latin: Shari' al-Amir Hamud bin 'Abd al-'Aziz (Prince Hamoud bin Abdulaziz Street)

notes: Green street-name board at a junction in Khobar, shot through a windscreen with a smudge over the left end (the last word العزيز and 'Pr' of Prince are partly veiled but readable). Distractor: blue arrow blade on the pole at right, 'طريق الأمير فيصل بن فهد بن عبدالعزيز / Prince Faisal Bin Fahd Bin Abdulaziz Rd.' (small), and a store fascia behind.

author: Geektaker

notes: Raised gold condensed letters on a white fascia, Riyadh, shot from below at a steep angle so the line rises to the right. The small text under the open-book logo at right (probably 'Ministry of Education' wording) is not legible and not transcribed.

author: amanderson2
attribution: Photo: amanderson2, CC BY 2.0, via Flickr. Source: https://www.flickr.com/photos/49399018@N00/51943919014. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Green lane plate with arabesque border on a coral-stone wall in Al-Balad, historic Jeddah. Lane number given in Arabic-Indic digits (٨٨) on the Arabic line and Western (88) on the English line. The Arabic name ends with dotless ى as written. Rust/dirt spots over 'Al-Jefri' and 'Lane' make the 'l' and 'n' look broken; small at 1600 px.
source_title: Door and Green Sign Al Balad Old Jeddah Saudi Arabia

author: Prof. Mortel
attribution: Photo: Prof. Mortel, CC BY 2.0, via Flickr. Source: https://www.flickr.com/photos/43714545@N06/50703478131. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Target is the fourth panel of a six-panel restoration-project sign stack in Al-Balad (historic Jeddah): building number in Arabic-Indic digits in brackets, then the house name. Other panels are distractors: Ministry of Culture / 'إدارة منطقة جده التاريخية' (spelled جده with ه), the Crown Prince restoration project text, 'المشروع رقم (٢)' (project no. 2), consultant 'مؤسسة التراث الخيرية' and contractor 'مؤسسة مباني الوطن التراثيه للمقاولات / NATIONAL HERITAGE BUILDINGS For Contracting'. Hoarding text behind is cut off.
source_title: Information sign regarding restoration of building in old Jeddah, Saudi Arabia

Wizarat ash-Shu'un al-Islamiya wa-d-Da'wa wa-l-Irshad (Ministry of Islamic Affairs, Da'wah and Guidance)

notes: Large white name board above the door of the Makkah Library building, sharp, slight upward angle. The two top-right ministry header lines are small. Year '١٣٧٠' uses Arabic-Indic digits. The Urdu and Persian lines are transcribed with Persian kaf (ک) and yeh (ی, final form undotted) and plain heh (ه); a checker should treat ك/ک, ي/ی/ى and ه/ہ as equivalent there since the glyphs do not settle the code points. Ministry logo at top centre. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.
